entries.ruling_text_verbatim: RATIFIED with changes. The seam at MT 21:18/21:19 (= WEB 21:13/21:14) goes onto the primaries' disclosed-triage list, and P04-008's confidence high goes with it. Verified by this execution: pmarks Ezek.21.18 PE (21.17 and 21.19 carry no mark); MT 21:18 ends נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (WEB 21:13 'says the Lord Yahweh.'), listed by ezek_device_inventory under utterance_of_the_lord_yhwh; MT 21:19 opens וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א (WEB 21:14 'You therefore, son of man, prophesy,'), listed under son_of_man_address; MT 21:17 opens זְעַ֤ק וְהֵילֵל֙ בֶּן אָדָ֔ם (WEB 21:12 'Cry and wail, son of man;'), so the row's SRA label at 21:18 is byte-false (S3-01). CHANGES: (1) the triage entry carries the pmarks lookup, both verses' bytes dual, and the comparison the primaries must weigh from both sides (OW-3): the strategy's own internal parent seam at 3:27/4:1 is drawn on this shape (refrain close plus mark, then 'and you, son of man'), and the corpus rule stated at P08-002 treats a refrain-grade close followed by a sub-onset as a seam candidate; against it stands whatever byte continuity the FIXUP-3 author argues (the sword figure running from MT 21:13 to 21:22, or another verse reason). (2) The primaries state a reason from both sides for keeping or cutting, and state whether confidence high survives the disclosed interior seam candidate; a fix-up never decides it (#e4 FIXUP-1 (3)). (3) The p04 orders say in words that the author's restated SRA is an argument, not a ruling, and does not pre-empt the primaries; the author who believes a cut is warranted reports it outside the row. Span and confidence unchanged through FIXUP-3.
